requirement: Dead-code detection: every tested feature is actually called in the production pipeline; green tests without a caller are false safety. A production call site is not sufficient: the control must be able to fire under production configuration, so its trigger conditions must reference state that exists in production (columns, tables, flags, platform capabilities). An invoked-but-unsatisfiable control — a phantom schema, a silently absent platform dependency — is the same false safety signal as dead code. Verification: a negative live probe, or a trace of the trigger conditions against production state.
